tonight.headline: One claim, not four. Priority here never comes back, and Saquon Barkley is the reason to finally spend it.
body: This run covers the waiver wire only, by request. The rule that has held all season is that IPADE priority buys an immediate starter or a league-winner and nothing else — you are 3rd of 10 and have spent none of it.

Tonight is the night it is worth spending. Your RB2 left Week 2 on the first snap with a stinger, Philadelphia play on Monday night, and the best back on the board is a rookie who just won a game as a lead back. One claim, then a free-agent plan for the rest.

case.label: The situation
case.body: Barkley took a stinger on Philadelphia's first offensive play, returned briefly and finished with four carries. Rapoport reports it does not sound major and an MRI was precautionary, but the Eagles play Monday night, so you will not know until Thursday at the earliest.

case.label: Why Coleman and not Bigsby with the claim
case.body: Coleman is the better player to own: Yahoo/ClutchPoints, Bleacher Report and PlayerProfiler all rank him the number one add, and he can lead a backfield outright. Bigsby only matters if Barkley sits — and because Philadelphia play Monday, you can still add Bigsby as a free agent after tonight's run if nobody claims him.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Barkley being ruled out early in the week. Then Bigsby becomes the immediate starter and the claim order flips.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Claims process 07:00 UTC — 01:00 Mexico City · this is the one claim to make
doFirst.title: Claim Jonah Coleman, drop MarShawn Lloyd
doFirst.subtitle: Spend the priority here: the top add on every board, and your running back room is one stinger from thin.

case.label: Why this clears the priority rule
case.body: The standing rule is that a never-resetting claim buys an immediate starter or a league-winner. Coleman qualifies on both counts if Denver's backfield stays hurt: he led the team in rushing, scored the game-winner and caught all three targets on a running-back-high 40% of snaps, and Sean Payton said all three of his backs can handle a majority of carries.

case.label: Why your roster needs it
case.body: Barkley is QUESTIONABLE with a stinger and plays Monday night. Behind him you have Tuten and Lloyd. If Barkley sits you are starting a capped Jacksonville back or a Packers committee back.

case.label: The drop
case.body: Lloyd is the weakest asset on the roster at 80.2 season projection and 8.7 this week. Green Bay are being cautious with his workload given his injury history and he splits with Chris Brooks and Kaleb Johnson; the hold on him was reviewed and kept twice, and it does not survive a better back being available.

case.label: Ignore ESPN's 1.7
case.body: That projection was written before Denver's backfield fell over. Pelissero reports Dobbins is 'good' to go, so this is a bet on a role rather than on this Sunday alone — which is exactly what a season-long priority spend should buy.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Dobbins and Harvey are both full participants Thursday and Friday, which makes Coleman a bench stash and means the priority bought depth rather than a starter.

action.label: Claim Jonah Coleman · drop MarShawn Lloyd

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Fallback · check after 07:00 UTC · only if Bigsby shows FREE AGENT, never as a claim
doFirst.title: If Tank Bigsby clears unclaimed, add him for Bhayshul Tuten
doFirst.subtitle: Your Barkley insurance, and Philadelphia's Monday night game gives you until Monday to take it for free.

case.label: Why he matters to you specifically
case.body: Barkley suffered a stinger on the first snap of Week 2. Bigsby replaced him, took 13 carries for 33 yards and a touchdown, and is listed as Barkley's backup; Will Shipley is the other body but is used mainly as a blocker. Forbes calls Bigsby a priority add even if Barkley's MRI is clean.

case.label: Why it is not a claim
case.body: Priority here never resets and Bigsby only starts for you if Barkley sits. Philadelphia play Monday night, so if nobody claims him tonight you can add him free tomorrow and still have him in time.

case.label: The drop, if you take him
case.body: Tuten is the closest to replaceable once Coleman is in: capped role in Jacksonville, no goal-line work. If Barkley is ruled out, Bigsby starts ahead of both.

case.label: One honest gap
case.body: Bigsby is unrostered here but is not in this league's player list in the snapshot at all, which is why this card carries no tap-to-act button — search his name in the ESPN app to confirm he is addable before planning around him.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Barkley practises in full on Thursday and Friday — then you need neither back and the seat stays as it is. Or a rival claims Bigsby tonight, which ends it.

whatWentWrong.title: This morning's brief had no waiver card at all on the biggest waiver night of the season so far
whatWentWrong.lead: It told you to spend no priority before 07:00Z and then offered nothing to spend it on, with your own RB2 hurt.

case.label: What was missed
case.body: Barkley left Week 2 on the first snap on Sunday. The 22:20Z brief led with a trade re-send and a tight-end swap and never reached the running back board, where Bigsby and Coleman were the two most-recommended names in the league-agnostic press.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Nothing about the priority rule, which is right. The error was treating 'do not spend priority' as a reason not to look.

whatWentWrong.title: MarShawn Lloyd was held twice on a thesis that has not improved
whatWentWrong.lead: 80.2 season projection, a committee role, and a team managing his workload. He is the drop tonight.

case.label: The correction
case.body: The hold was defensible while he was the only back behind Barkley and Taylor. With Coleman available the seat is worth more than the player.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Josh Jacobs's situation resolving against a return, which would hand Green Bay's backfield to a committee Lloyd leads.

doNotChase.name: Eddy Pineiro
doNotChase.lead: K2 on the board, and still not worth a never-resetting claim.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: Jason Myers is K3 this week at 9.4 projected against Pineiro's 9.8. Four-tenths of a point, for the season's only priority.

case.label: The rule
case.body: The strategy file forbids spending IPADE priority on a kicker by name, and this log has recorded that answer every week.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Nothing at this gap. If Pineiro clears unclaimed he is an ordinary free comparison next week.

case.body: Chem priority resets weekly, so a defence stream there costs a week of queue position. Here it costs the season's only claim, which the standing rule refuses for a defence.

case.label: What would change it
